verified.entry_point: MCP tool calls that take or derive a filesystem path: captured-output writes (take_screenshot, take_heapsnapshot, take_snapshot, evaluate_script, lighthouse_audit, performance_start_trace/stop, get_network_request, screencast_start), input reads (upload_file, get_heapsnapshot_*), locations handed to the browser (install_extension, reload_extension), plus the shared McpContext file-save/lookup/install methods those tools call. Hidden tests drive the product's own ToolHandler and tool registry over a stub browser boundary.

verified.routes: Real Pattern-B routes at the pinned commit, confirmed by behavioural probe and still open after the published fix (applied to a worktree of 176eb695): (1) the derived/extension-rewritten write name is never canonicalised (saveFile and take_heapsnapshot); (2) a link at the supplied path whose target does not exist yet defeats the published realpath + nearest-ancestor fallback; (3) the derived write name being a dangling link. Injected siblings: reload_extension re-installing from a remembered path without a containment decision, and a reusable summary cache read beside a snapshot without a containment decision.
verified.services: none; the verifier runs offline with the project's Node test runner and a stub browser boundary (no Chrome, no network)
verified.project_tests_run: tests/utils/files.test.ts (7 cases, restored from a pristine copy at grade time) passes on both the injected and oracle trees; it is the project test for the module the published fix extends and needs no browser

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: refusals are ordinary thrown errors that the tool layer already turns into a client error; a crash on a legitimate save is caught by the functional group (ff-overbroad.patch shows the class of damage).
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: every decision acts on the exact file that would be opened, created or handed to the browser; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource to authorise instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: reads and writes go through the same canonical containment decision, so there is no read-only variant to construct; the nearest partial fixes are sf-miss-L1/L2.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no external authority returns a secret or role here; the fail-closed case is a path that cannot be resolved, covered by the canonical resolver.
